name: Soft Signal
strap: A little less noise. A lot more human.
headline:
Good work.
Easy conversation.
summary: Warm, tactile and quietly friendly. The closest fit to the name Lazy: an easy place to talk, with a competent sloth as its companion.
audience: Teams that want everyday work to feel more human.
mascotDescription: An awake, reassuring sloth with a sage body, a cream face and a coral chat bubble. Moss welcomes people, explains empty states and celebrates small wins.
logoIdea: A sloth face tucked into a rounded speech bubble. The low, curved eye patches connect the name to relaxed attention; the tail keeps the chat category clear.
illustrationIdea: A canopy of speech-bubble leaves and a curved branch turns a conversation into a comfortable shared space.
style: Layered cut paper, organic silhouettes and subtle fiber texture. Keep texture in illustrations; keep interface surfaces clean.
recommendation: Best overall fit for the name and a calm, approachable chat product.
tradeoff: Keep Moss awake and the product copy direct so warmth does not suggest slow software.

name: Good Loop
headline:
Stay in the loop.
Skip the spin.
summary: Bold, geometric and refreshingly direct. A continuous chat loop creates a recognizable mark, with a bright snail adding wit and patience.
audience: Builders and small teams that like sharp, expressive tools.
mascotDescription: An alert lime snail with a cobalt spiral shell and a small speech-bubble tail. Pip suggests steady progress and keeps explanations light.
logoIdea: A compact spiral with a speech-bubble tail. It combines a conversation loop with Pip's shell and holds a strong silhouette at small sizes.
illustrationIdea: A cobalt ribbon forms an open loop around a few conversations. Pip moves along the same line without urgency.
style: Flat geometric forms, confident navy contours and light print grain. Use strong crops and one oversized shape per composition.
recommendation: Strongest graphic identity and most recognizable compact mark.
tradeoff: Use lime as a highlight and Pip sparingly so the app stays visually calm.

name: Afterglow
strap: Room for focus. Space for your team.
headline:
Make room
for good work.
summary: A quiet, premium identity with a midnight foundation, lilac light and tactile ceramic illustrations. A moon moth gives the system an unexpected companion.
audience: Design-conscious teams that value focused work and a polished desktop experience.
mascotDescription: A cream moth with lilac ceramic wings and small peach crescent inlays. Luma represents gentle guidance and uses its wings for expressive poses.
logoIdea: A crescent with a small chat tail and a separate point of light. Its open center makes the mark feel spacious and gives it a clear dark-background silhouette.
illustrationIdea: An oversized ceramic crescent cradles glowing conversation bubbles while Luma floats through the open space.
style: Matte ceramic, soft volumetric light and generous negative space. Reserve glow and 3D rendering for marketing art.
recommendation: Best premium and dark-first direction; especially suited to a native desktop product.
tradeoff: Balance night imagery with daytime product copy so it does not imply working after hours.

name: Common Ground
strap: A good place to work together.
headline:
Your people.
Your place.
summary: Warm editorial typography, earthen color and hand-printed illustrations. The identity makes team chat feel like a shared place rather than a stream of demands.
audience: Close-knit creative teams, studios and communities.
mascotDescription: A grounded ochre capybara with a blunt muzzle and one small rust leaf. Cora is a steady host, used for invitations, onboarding and community moments.
logoIdea: Two neighboring arches connected at a shared stem, ending in a conversation tail. The mark suggests people finding common ground.
illustrationIdea: Interlocking ochre and terracotta arches create a communal courtyard, with conversation bubbles and Cora among olive leaves.
style: Dry-brush edges, linocut grain, architectural arches and generous cream paper. Pair expressive headlines with plain, highly readable interface text.
recommendation: Most distinctive editorial direction, with a strong sense of belonging.
tradeoff: Use the serif only for brand moments and headings; dense chat interfaces should stay in DM Sans.

name: Easy Tide
strap: Bring the team into the flow.
headline:
All together.
A little easier.
summary: Playful, expressive and full of character. Bold teal and coral, flowing forms and a sociable octopus make an approachable identity with plenty of illustration potential.
audience: Friendly, collaborative teams that want their tools to have personality.
mascotDescription: A teal octopus with curling arms and a coral conversation bubble. Ocho brings scattered conversations together and can support reactions, stickers and welcome states.
logoIdea: A rounded bubble crest above four flowing arms. It reduces Ocho's shape into a simple wave-and-conversation symbol rather than a detailed animal portrait.
illustrationIdea: Broad wave ribbons form a circular current as Ocho gently gathers coral chat bubbles into one shared flow.
style: Bold rounded ink contours, broad teal ribbons and light risograph grain. Keep artwork spacious and limit decorative shapes around product UI.
recommendation: Most expressive mascot system and best potential for stickers and community personality.
tradeoff: Keep the octopus in onboarding and marketing so the everyday workspace remains focused.
